description.narrative: BIRN Albania is a non-governmental media organization. This is an un-earmarked support to the Strategic Plan 2021-2025. Through high quality investigative reporting and a pool of skilled journalists, BIRN Albania examines and scrutinizes key processes, promotes debates and provides the public with impartial and reliable information. By making available data and public documents, BIRN will enable journalists and researchers to be in a better position to hold institutions and policymakers accountable in the progress made for the implementation of the commitments taken in the fight against organized crime and corruption. BIRN Albania will support journalists’ coverage from the regions, to bring the voice of the voiceless in the national debate and the public sphere, particularly for abuses linked with the environment and stories that provide a gender perspective. BIRN Albania will work with experts, donors and partners to strengthen its procedures in terms of gender mainstreaming, the integration of environment perspective, data protection and privacy.

BIRN Albania är en icke-statlig medieorganisation. Detta är ett icke öronmärkt stöd till den strategiska planen 2021–2025. Genom undersökande rapportering av hög kvalitet och en pool av skickliga journalister undersöker och granskar BIRN Albanien nyckelprocesser, främjar debatter och förser allmänheten med opartisk och tillförlitlig information. Genom att tillgängliggöra data och offentliga dokument kommer BIRN att göra det möjligt för journalister och forskare att vara i en bättre position för att hålla institutioner och beslutsfattare ansvariga för de framsteg som görs för att genomföra de åtaganden som gjorts i kampen mot organiserad brottslighet och korruption. BIRN Albania kommer att stödja journalisters bevakning från regionerna, för att föra fram de röstlösa i den nationella debatten och i det offentliga rummet, särskilt för övergrepp kopplade till miljön och berättelser som ger ett jämställdhetsperspektiv. BIRN Albania kommer att arbeta med experter, givare och partners för att stärka sina förfaranden när det gäller jämställdhetsintegrering, integrering av miljöperspektiv, dataskydd och integritet.

The objective of the intervention is that Albanian society upholds democratic values and freedoms allowing citizens equal opportunities to make informed choices and hold government accountable. The desired changes that BIRN Albania aims to achieve through its core programme during the period 2021 2025 are the following: 1) People have increased access to accurate information; 2) People have increased influence on democratic process: 3) People have increased opportunities to claim their rights; 4) Internal capacities of the organization are strengthened.

description.narrative:
OUTCOME 1: People have increased access to accurate information
BIRN Albania expanded citizens access to accurate, timely, and pluralistic information while maintaining investigative depth and editorial independence.
- Reporter.al registered more than 20 million page views, while the organisations Facebook platforms generated over 57.5 million impressions and more than 5.2 million video views, confirming BIRN Albania's position as one of the most visible independent public-interest media actors in the country.
- Editorial production targets were surpassed. During 2021-2025, BIRN Albania published 6,988 articles, including 153 investigations, 1,864 in-depth features and analyses, 4,971 news pieces and more than 203 data-rich stories, substantially exceeding the original strategic targets. Coverage of electoral processes was ensured through the development of four live blogs and dedicated election subpages covering the parliamentary elections of 2021 and 2025, the local elections of 2023 and the Himara by-election.
- Over the strategy period, 337 journalists were trained on investigative and specialised reporting topics including organised crime, money laundering, environment, digital rights, data journalism and elections. Eighteen open calls were launched to support investigative and in-depth reporting, resulting in 80 journalists receiving investigative grants and producing at least 74 investigations. Overall, more than 60 Albanian journalists supported by the programme produced over 2,015 articles and 151 videos, while more than 208 journalists, students and researchers benefited from on-the-job mentoring and editorial support. Specialised training curricula on organised crime and money laundering and on environment and climate reporting were developed and published, alongside additional modules on data protection, monitoring and evaluation and investigative techniques.
OUTCOME 2: People have increased influence on democratic process
Reporting and transparency tools strengthened citizens influence on democratic processes through sustained monitoring of corruption, justice reform implementation, organised crime, and political finance transparency.
- Large-scale publication of FOI-based documentation and structured datasets strengthened access to information across sectors including procurement, political finance, justice reform and asset recovery. Continuous monitoring of the vetting process and the functioning of institutions such as the High Judicial Council, High Prosecutorial Council and SPAK ensured that justice reform remained subject to public scrutiny not only during the vetting cycle but also in the critical phase of institutional consolidation and high-profile investigations. The launch of Albania's first Criminal Assets Database and specialised reporting on confiscation practices and illicit financial flows strengthened evidence-based debate on the effectiveness of the country's response to organised crime and money laundering.
- Investigative reporting contributed to the exposure of dozens of corruption and abuse-of-power cases, generated sustained public and institutional reactions, and supported the initiation of official investigations and indictments in several high-profile cases, including those related to public-private partnerships. Through its integrated approach linking transparency infrastructure, justice reform monitoring and specialised reporting on organised crime risks, BIRN Albania strengthened citizens access to actionable information and reinforced its role as a central accountability actor supporting democratic oversight and rule-of-law reforms in Albania.
OUTCOME 3: People have increased opportunities to claim their rights
Cooperation with civil society organisations, activists, local media, and international partners contributed to strengthening pluralism, defending media freedom, and addressing emerging risks related to disinformation, foreign information manipulation, and digital-sphere vulnerabilities.
- Through joint dialogue platforms, mentoring support and grant-based cooperation schemes, BIRN Albania expanded the network of organisations contributing to evidence-based reporting on elections, environmental governance, human rights, disinformation and financial transparency.
- BIRN Albania ensured that the voices of underreported and vulnerable groups remained visible in national debate through sustained investigative reporting, documentary storytelling, community-level engagement and thematic monitoring of identity-based discrimination and manipulation narratives. Reporting on gender-based violence, migration, minority rights, disability inclusion and access to social services linked lived experiences to systemic governance challenges and strengthened evidence-based advocacy efforts. Structured monitoring of identity-based disinformation further expanded this work by documenting how narratives targeting women, LGBTIQ communities and minority groups influence Albania's information environment and democratic discourse.
- Across the strategy period, BIRN Albania expanded its role from documenting individual violations in Albanias information space to building a structured monitoring and research framework addressing attacks on journalists, regulatory transparency risks, electoral disinformation and foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI). Through research reports, electoral media monitoring studies, national advocacy campaigns and cooperation with partner organisations and professional networks, BIRN contributed to strengthening the resilience of Albania's media environment and supported informed engagement with European standards related to media pluralism and democratic integrity.
OUTCOME 4: Internal capacities of the organization strengthened
Significant progress was made in strengthening BIRN Albania's organisational resilience through improvements in governance systems, monitoring and evaluation frameworks, compliance procedures, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity practices, gender mainstreaming integration, and preparation of the organisations 2026-2030 strategy.
- The strengthened monitoring and evaluation framework introduced during the strategy period ensures that programme performance can be tracked more systematically across thematic areas and funding instruments.
-The development of internal policies and compliance procedures, including gender-mainstreaming planning tools, environmental-sustainability integration measures and personal-data-protection regulations, has institutionalised standards that will remain operational across future programme
- Investments in digital infrastructure, cybersecurity preparedness and specialised monitoring databases significantly strengthened BIRN Albania's long-term investigative and analytical capacity. Upgraded editorial platforms, strengthened data-management procedures and improved cyber-resilience training ensure that the organisation can continue to operate securely while managing increasingly complex datasets related to elections, media pluralism, disinformation and organised crime.
- The development of structured procedures for managing partnerships and sub-granting schemes represents an important institutional asset for future programme implementation. These procedures enable BIRN Albania to operate effectively within consortium-based actions and to support local civil society and media actors through transparent and accountable funding-forwarding mechanisms aligned with EU and network standards.
- The organisational learning generated through the external evaluation process and its management response directly informed preparation of the upcoming 2026-2030 strategy.
